grades.clinical_supported: Systematic review and/or EMA well-established use supports a specific indication (efficacy still often modest; product-specific).
grades.clinical_mixed: Clinical trials exist but a systematic review judged them inconsistent, low quality or insufficient.
grades.traditional_only: Accepted by EMA HMPC on the basis of long-standing (traditional) use only; efficacy not shown in adequate trials.
grades.monograph_area_only: EMA lists an adopted EU monograph in this therapeutic area, but the public page had no summary stating whether use is traditional or well-established; treat as at most traditional until the monograph PDF is read.
grades.not_endorsed: EMA HMPC issued a public statement instead of a monograph (no use endorsed).
grades.no_known_benefit: No EMA HMPC monograph and no Cochrane review located for this plant in our search; no evidence-based medicinal use known to this pack.

general_safety.text: Herbal medicines are not available on the NHS. NHS advises not taking herbal medicines if pregnant or breastfeeding, with kidney or liver problems, or with certain medicines (statins, antidepressants, metformin, ramipril, warfarin, combined pill), and to check with a pharmacist first.
In the UK a traditional herbal registration (THR) is granted only for minor conditions not needing medical supervision; NHS advises checking for the THR mark and an MHRA product code.
Suspected side effects of herbal medicines can be reported to the MHRA Yellow Card scheme.
For suspected plant poisoning, seek urgent medical help and take a sample of the plant (RHS); NHS poisoning guidance applies.
